correctness.rationale: Re-audited RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and check_spl_divisibility.py under /workspace/repairs/5/. The original decimals stated for θ*, r*, and r_z have incorrect terminal digits; the exact polynomial definitions and proof survive. With r=1/(1+θ) and a=(1+r)/r, summing (a+|k|)r^|k| at t=0 gives a(1+r)/(1−r)+2r/(1−r)² and confirms the normalizer. Applying a+r∂_r to the Poisson kernel, with a a multiplier rather than a differentiated factor, gives the claimed numerator A+B cos t. Expanding verifies B=2(2r³+r²−1), A+B>0 on (0,1), and A−B=−(1+r)²(r³+3r²−r−1)/r. Descartes' rule and the signs at 0 and 1 show that the cubic has a unique positive root r_z and that φ(π) is zero there and negative beyond it; a symmetric infinitely divisible characteristic function cannot be zero or negative. For r<r_z one has A>|B|. The unique real |s|<1 satisfying B/A=2s/(1+s²) factors the numerator; subtracting the absolutely convergent logarithmic series of the denominator yields masses [2r^n+(−1)^(n+1)s^n]/n at each of ±n. Lattice infinite divisibility requires these masses to be nonnegative: |φ(2π)|=1 forces zero Gaussian part and integer support of the Lévy measure, whose total mass off 0 is finite, and symmetry removes drift. Uniqueness of Fourier coefficients then gives the necessity; the summable nonnegative expansion itself gives sufficiency. All masses are positive for |s|≤r, and |s|>r gives negative even coefficients eventually. The monotone transform 2s/(1+s²) and the exact comparisons B(1+r²)+2rA=2r(1−r²)² and B(1+r²)−2rA=2P(r) prove s>−r and the upper bound iff P≤0. P has one positive root and 2P(r_z)=A(1−r_z)²>0, so r*<r_z. At equality s=r and no Lévy mass vanishes. Direct fractions at r=27/40 verify A−B=166093/69120000>0 and, for w=41/50, B(1+w²)−2wA=5544383/8640000000 and w⁴−2r⁴=29546783/800000000, giving a strict negative fourth log harmonic despite positivity of the characteristic function. Numerical replay is exact: the consecutive 10^(−20) brackets starting at 0.67454183542439917437 and 0.67513087056664607088 have polynomial signs (−,+) by rational arithmetic. Transform their endpoints in reverse order by r↦1/r−1 to certify θ*=0.482487738319200658… and θ_z=0.481194304092015622…. Opposite signs fail for the intervals denoted by the old exact prefixes. The corrected checker now uses these exact brackets and avoids displaying extra digits from a machine-precision solve. The shipped scripts were inspected, not executed; an independent rational calculation replayed the bracket and witness identities.

Ordinary one-sided Poisson–Lindley and a difference of two such counts are also different constructions, not aliases for symmetrizing one mass.

value.rationale: The exact phase answers when a named bilateral count law admits a compound-Poisson construction and specifies every signed-integer jump rate in the permitted regime. Two provably distinct nearby roots show why a positive characteristic function is not an adequate diagnostic in this family; the rational witness separates them without relying on digits. The value is this structural boundary and distinction in a published family, not merely finer numerical accuracy or an example of a generally known zero-free phenomenon. The corrected decimal prefixes change neither the theorem nor its scope.
